Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the second essay! Some final instructions are being given by Oscar Jackson in the huddle of New Zealand Under-19. They are followed by the two openers of Pakistan Under-19, Shahzaib Khan and Shamyl Hussain. Matt Rowe has the new ball in hand and he is raring to go. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

New Zealand Under-19 had a shaky start as the top-order batters failed to provide a proper start to their team and they lost their first three wickets in just 7 overs. The skipper, Oscar Jackson, and Ollie Tewatiya started a firm partnership but it went down the hill as well. After the arrival of Lachlan Stackpole, the Kiwis were looking a bit easy as a few knocks from him absolutely changed the momentum of the game. Ollie Tewatiya, on the other hand, was trying to provide as much of the strike to his partner. They were set in the crease and formed an important partnership of 61 runs off 65 deliveries, but it got broken with the dismissal of Stackpole. He missed out on his half-century as well for just 8 runs. After this, the Kiwis lost wickets one after the other. No one from the lower middle order was able to hang around. The tail-enders couldn't help much and ended up putting 140 on the board to defend. They have the resources to make a match out of this. Can the Kiwi bowlers succeed in doing so? We shall find out.

Ubaid Shah is up for a chat. He says that he was concentrating on length ball as guided by their bowling coach, and that's what he did. He continues that he is confident enough with his batting unit and he reckons that they will get the runs.

A sensational bowling performance from Pakistan Under-19! They never allowed New Zealand Under-19 to breathe easy and kept coming at them and have bowled them out for 140. They started well with the ball in the first Powerplay all thanks to Ubaid Shah as he accounted for the top three batters of their opposition. Mohammad Zeeshan and Naveed Khan did their job the cleaning the middle order and special credit to Naveen who broke the partnership of Lachlan Stackpole and Ollie Tewatiya, which was looking set and dangerous. Ali Asfand and Arafat Minhas joined hands to wrap things up quickly to take care of the lower middle order. There were a couple of misfields in the middle overs but that did not cost them much. Ubaid Shah and Arafat Minhas managed to pick up three wickets each. Naveed Khan picked two wickets while Ali Asfand and Mohammad Zeeshan chipped in with one each. It is a modest total to chase for the Pakistani batters, but we have seen crazy things happening in this tournament.

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! On a fullish length, tailing in, at the toes, Snehith Reddy misses the tickle and the ball comes off the pads. The keeper, Saad Baig dives away to his left and makes a half-stop to keep it to just a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Ahmad Hassan to Snehith Reddy, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Easy pickings! Errs in line and length does Hassan as this is full and sliding on the pads, Snehith Reddy lets the ball come to him and clips it through square leg for an easy boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Ahmad Hassan to Snehith Reddy, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Goes full and shapes it away from the batter, Snehith Reddy covers his off-stump and leaves the ball alone.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Ahmad Hassan to Snehith Reddy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Not in complete control but they all count! Ubaid Shah lands it on a short of a length and swinging away, outside off, Tom Jones throws his hands at the delivery and gets an outside edge that flies over the slip cordon for a boundary. It almost went the distance for a maximum.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Ubaid Shah to Tom Jones, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Keeps it on a back of a length, on off, Tom Jones gets on the front foot and bunts it towards short cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Ubaid Shah to Tom Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angles it in, on a back of a length, on off, Tom Jones opens the bat face and steers it with soft hands towards backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Ubaid Shah to Tom Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A bit too straight, on a length, on the pads, Snehith Reddy helps it away with the angle but Ahmad Hassan at fine leg is standing quite fine and it will be just a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Ubaid Shah to Snehith Reddy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On the off-stump line, full as well, Snehith Reddy defends it out with a straight bat back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Ubaid Shah to Snehith Reddy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches it right up to the batter, on off, Snehith Reddy stays balanced in his crease and presses forward to firm the drive towards cover. The fielder dives to his left and takes the sting out of the ball but cannot prevent the batters from running two.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Ubaid Shah to Snehith Reddy, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Serves it on a back of a length, around off, Tom Jones rides the bounce and punches it along the ground towards cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Ahmad Hassan to Tom Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: This is bowled from wide of the crease and it is angled in, full and around off, Tom Jones reads it well and pats it down the wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Ahmad Hassan to Tom Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full again and swinging away, outside off, Tom Jones does not go chasing at the delivery and lets it go through to the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Ahmad Hassan to Tom Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Width on offer and Tom Jones cashes in! Hassan gets the ball to swing away from the batter, on a length, outside off, Tom Jones lets the ball come to him and opens the bat face to drive it square and past point for the second boundary of the over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Ahmad Hassan to Tom Jones, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Adjusts his length by bowling it on a good length, on off, Tom Jones prods forward and stabs it down on the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Ahmad Hassan to Tom Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Shot of the morning so far! Ahmad Hassan hurls it a bit too full, outside off, Tom Jones picks up the length early and leans into the drive. Creams it through covers for his first boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Ahmad Hassan to Tom Jones, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Shaping away, full and outside off, Snehith Reddy watches it all the way through and is happy to leave the ball alone. End of a successful over from Ubaid Shah.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Ubaid Shah to Snehith Reddy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Snehith Reddy is in at number 3 for New Zealand Under-19.

OUT! CASTLED! Ubaid Shah with the first strike for Pakistan Under-19! Luke Watson goes without troubling the scorers! Ubaid Shah gets his radar right this time and hits the target this time, full and swinging in, on off, Luke Watson is caught on the crease and reaches out in front with his hands. The ball nips back in off the deck and brushes his back pad before going on to uproot the off-stump.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Ubaid Shah to Luke Watson, OUT! b Ubaid Shah.

Commentary.Commentary: Drags his length back and slants it across the left-hander, on off, Luke Watson drops his gloves and sways away to let the ball go.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Ubaid Shah to Luke Watson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FIVE WIDES! Wayward from Ubaid Shah! Goes searching for that magical delivery but slips it down leg, on a fullish length, Luke Watson fails to tickle it fine and the keeper, Saad Baig fails to get to it despite the dive to his right.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Ubaid Shah to Luke Watson, 5 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: A bit of inward movement there, on a length, on middle and leg, Luke Watson stays rooted in his crease to work it across the line but closes the bat face early. Gets a soft leading that rolls to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Ubaid Shah to Luke Watson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Continues from over the wicket and gets the ball to angle away from the left-hander, on a length, outside off, Luke Watson does not cover his off stump and lifts his bat to let the ball pass.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length, on off, Luke Watson waits back in his crease and pushes it out with a straight bat back to the bowler.

Commentary.Commentary: Well bowled! Surprises the batter by getting the ball to tail back in sharply, full in length, on middle, Tom Jones is waiting for the ball to go away from him and gets caught into a tangle. However, he adjusts well and gets his bat in front of the left toe to keep this one out.

Commentary.Commentary: Play and a miss! Goes wide of the crease does Hassan and bowls it on a length, a bit wide outside off, Tom Jones tries to cash in on the width but connects with thin air.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Ahmad Hassan to Tom Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Serves it on a back of a length, around off, Tom Jones hangs back and knocks it from the crease to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Ahmad Hassan to Tom Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Beauty! Goes full this time and gets the ball to swing away from the right-hander, Tom Jones gets lured forward in defence but the ball goes away to beat him on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Ahmad Hassan to Tom Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Goes slightly full and gets the ball to nip away a bit, on the sixth stump line, Tom Jones is a bit tentative on the front foot as he pushes it out to backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Ahmad Hassan to Tom Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Lands it on a back of a length from over the wicket, outside off, Tom Jones stands tall and punches it along the ground to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Ahmad Hassan to Tom Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Who will bowl from the other end? It will be Ahmad Hassan. He is also starting with two slips in place.

Offers a bit of width on off and swinging away, short of a length, Tom Jones plays it late and runs it down to third man for a single to open his account. Tom Jones and New Zealand Under-19 are underway!

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length, on off, Tom Jones gets on top of the bounce and extends his arms to dab it along the ground to backward point.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches it up in search of swing, in the channel on off, Tom Jones offers no shot at it and leaves the ball alone.

Commentary.Commentary: Drags his length back a touch and bowls it on off, shaping in as well, Tom Jones gets his front foot across and hops to pat it to the right of the bowler.

Commentary.Commentary: This is angled into the batter, on a length, on off, Tom Jones presses forward and gets his bat out in front to defend it down the wicket.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts from over the wicket and gets the ball to shape away from the right-hander, on a back of a length, outside off, Tom Jones watchfully shoulders arms to the delivery.

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the national anthems. Grey skies greet the two umpires as they make their way out to the middle. Pakistan Under-19 are in a huddle near the ropes before they spread out to take their respective field positions. It will be Tom Jones and Luke Watson to open the innings for New Zealand Under-19. Ubaid Shah will start off the proceedings with the new ball. for Pakistan Under-19. Here we go...

The first ball in this blockbuster clash is moments away but before that, the match officials and the two teams will line up for their respective national anthems. It will be New Zealand's national anthem first followed by the national anthem of Pakistan.

PITCH REPORT - Andrew Leonard is near the deck. He starts by saying that it is very overcast and the conditions are very similar to that of the game between Afghanistan and New Zealand. Marina Iqbal joins him and says that this pitch has been used for a couple of games. Feels that this wicket is softer and reckons that the ball will grip in the surface. Adds that these are ideal conditions for pacers. She also says that batters will have to be wary about where their off-stump is and try to keep the bat close to the body.

The captain of Pakistan Under-19, Saad Baig says that it is not a bad toss to lose. States that they will look to play quality cricket and will give their best. Mentions that they are not taking any extra pressure but they know that this is an important game. Ends by saying that looking at the conditions they have made one change with Naveed Khan coming in for Khubaib Khalil.

The skipper of New Zealand Under-19, Oscar Jackson says that they will bat first. Mentions that the pitch looks pretty hard and reckons that the conditions will remain the same throughout the day. Feels that runs on the board will be important. Informs that they have made two changes to the team that played the last game. Ends by saying that he hopes that the overhead conditions stay the same and the ball swings later in the game as well.

New Zealand Under-19 (Playing XI) - Luke Watson, Tom Jones, Snehith Reddy (In for Robbie Foulkes), Ollie Tewatiya, Oscar Jackson (C), Lachlan Stackpole, Zac Cumming, Sam Clode (WK), Matt Rowe, Ryan Tsourgas, Mason Clarke (In for Ewald Schreuder) .

Pakistan Under-19 (Playing XI) - Shahzaib Khan, Shamyl Hussain, Azan Awais, Saad Baig (C/WK), Ahmad Hassan, Haroon Arshad, Arafat Minhas, Ubaid Shah, Mohammad Zeeshan, Naveed Khan (In for Khubaib Khalil), Ali Asfand.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in the favour of New Zealand Under-19 and they have opted to BAT first.

On the other hand, New Zealand Under-19 have also won two in two in the group stage, but their second win was a nervy one, which they would like to avoid in this game. Their batting unit is a bit inconsistent, as they performed outstandingly in the first match against Nepal, but the same unit almost made a mess while chasing a paltry total against the Afghans. But we might see some positive changes in it, as they had a good amount of time to rethink and return fresh. Their bowling unit has done a decent job in both matches and the skipper, Oscar Jackson, would like to continue it in this match as well. Who will continue their winning streak? And who will finish second in Group D? Let's find out! Toss and team news in a bit.

Pakistan Under-19 have been flawless throughout their campaign for the World Cup. They are currently sitting at the top of the table, as they have a slightly better run rate than the Kiwis. Shahzaib Khan will surely get some credit for Pak's recent performance, as he has scored 143 runs in two matches. Their bowling unit is also performing exceptionally well, and it would be tough for the Kiwi batters to face Ubaid Shah and Mohammad Zeeshan.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of match number 22 between Pakistan Under-19 and New Zealand Under-19 at Buffalo Park in East London. The stakes are high as both teams have booked their spots for the Super Six round, but they will fight for the top spot in Group D.
... MATCHDAY ...

We are awaiting match number 22 of the ICC Under-19 World Cup and we are at Buffalo Park in East London where Pakistan Under-19 will face New Zealand Under-19. Both teams are on the top of their game in this tournament so far and have won both their matches. Pakistan Under-19 stands at the top of the table with the better NRR. In their last outing against Nepal U-19, the bowling unit showed good rhythm. They used 7 bowlers and 6 bowlers scalped at least one wicket. Arafat Minhas was the pick of the bowlers with his three wickets. Ubaid Shah and Ahmad Hassan got two each with the rest of the three getting a wicket each. They managed to restrict the opposition to a low score which made things easier for their batters. Shamyl Hussain and Shahzaib Khan gave a strong start to the batting innings but a few quick dismissals put some pressure on them. The skipper, Saad Baig was dismissed for a duck but Azan Awais handled the innings well and played a dependable knock. He along with Haroon Arshad made sure that they finished the game on a strong note. New Zealand Under-19, on the other hand, are also having a very strong tournament so far but the team almost faltered in their last game against Afghanistan U-19. Matt Rowe clinched a brilliant fifer for the young Kiwis with some support from Ryan Tsourgas and Ewald Schreuder. A comprehensive bowling performance and some very quick wickets cleaned up their opposition for a mere 91 runs. However, their batting unit also faltered and almost lost the match. Only their skipper, Oscar Jackson and Lachlan Stackpole managed to put up double-digit scores, while the rest only managed to score in single digits. The target was low so they managed to chase it down but not after a very tough chase. They lost 9 wickets in the process. This will be a big concern for the team going into this match against a strong opposition. Which team are you supporting in this exciting encounter because one team will face its first defeat in this tournament?
